blocks.content:
CBI requires the consent of the concerned state government to investigate cases within that state.

Two types of consent exist:
• General Consent – Allows CBI to investigate without case-specific permission.
• Specific Consent – Required for each individual case.

However, the Supreme Court and High Courts can order a CBI investigation without state consent.

Difference between General and Specific Consent is a frequently asked objective question in Polity.
State consent requirement stems from the statutory provisions governing the functioning of the CBI.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: CBI must obtain state government consent before conducting investigations within a state's territorial jurisdiction.
General Consent grants the CBI standing permission to investigate cases without case-by-case approvals.
Specific Consent forces the CBI to seek explicit permission from the state government for every individual case.
The Supreme Court and High Courts hold constitutional authority to mandate CBI investigations without state consent.
